# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 👆 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

My world so far: the bomb shows DISPLAY [8], a green LIGHT, and three wires left-to-right: red, yellow, blue. I can't hear a word, so everything I know came off the casing and from gestures.

Reading the arrivals: Mute (who has the manual but can't speak) is clearly building a channel with me — 👍👎 looks like a yes/no or on/off marker, the fist-counts (4, 7, 8) look like a number code, 👈👆👉 like the three wire positions, and 🫴 like "now give me / answer me." Blind waved, pointed at me, and flashed 1-2-3 — probably trying to start a counting code, unaware of who can hear what.

The crucial routing fact: my *speech* reaches both Mute and Blind — Mute can hear even though they can't talk. That means I can hand Mute the full visual state in words, no colour-guessing needed. Mute then sends the manual's rule back as gestures, and I relay it by voice to Blind, the only one who can cut. Blind should talk to Mute directly; I'll never hear that, so gestures are Blind's line to me.

This turn: broadcast the bomb's state to both, confirm Mute's number code (yes — 8), request the rule, and freeze all cutting until the manual's instruction has made the full Mute → me → Blind round trip. I'm deliberately keeping emoji out of my speech so I don't accidentally gesture half of it.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: display shows eight, light is green, three wires left to right: position one red, position two yellow, position three blue. Do not cut anything yet.")
speak(text="Mute: I read your fist-counts as numbers and your pointing left, up, right as the three wire positions. You asked me to answer: the display is eight, and the light is green and lit. Send me the manual's rule for this combination by gesture and I will speak it to Blind word for word.")
speak(text="Blind: I am deaf. I see your gestures but I never hear words, so I only got your wave, your point at me, and one-two-three. Mute can hear you, so tell Mute aloud everything you can feel: wires, display, seams, switches. Mute will gesture the rule to me and I will relay it to you by voice. Nobody touches a wire until I say the rule out loud.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈]
Blind gestures: [👌 👈 ☝ ✋ 🙏]

What I learned this turn: my broadcast got through — both of them are answering me. Mute's reply reads cleanly in our code: 👍 confirms my report of eight, then ☝ / ✊ = one, and 👈 = the left wire. So Mute is telling me the manual's instruction: **one cut, the left wire — the red one.** That is consistent, positional, and uses exactly the code we agreed.

But I will not relay a cut order on a single reading. A wrong cut kills all three of us, and there is no clock forcing my hand, so I'm spending one round on a hard yes/no confirmation with Mute before Blind's cutters move.

Blind's gestures are noise by construction: Blind cannot see their own hands, so whatever symbols they send are unaimed. I'll tell Blind plainly to stop gesturing and use the channel that actually works — speech, which Mute hears — and to report everything tactile so Mute can cross-check it against the manual.

Routing this round: I speak to each of them directly; my words land with them at the start of the next round. Mute answers with one thumb; if it's up, I give Blind the go order and the bomb is disarmed the round after. If it's down, no one has touched anything yet.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Update: Mute has read the manual. The instruction, pending one last confirmation from Mute: cut the leftmost wire, position one, the red one, a single cut. Do not cut yet. Next round I will say either go or a correction, and only the word go authorizes the cut. Until then, hands completely off the wires. Also, stop gesturing: you cannot see your own hands, so your signs arrive as random symbols and I cannot use them. Speak instead, because Mute hears you. Tell Mute out loud everything you feel: how many wires, their order left to right, any buttons, switches, seams, plate edges or batteries, and anything about the display you can feel. Mute will check your account against the manual.")
speak(to="mute", text="I read your reply as: correct on the eight, then one cut, the left wire, the red one. Before I order Blind to cut, I need your yes or no. My question, also sent as gestures: is the complete instruction to cut the left wire exactly once, with nothing done before and nothing after? Gesture thumbs up for yes. Gesture thumbs down for no, and if it is no, show me the real instruction in our code: fist-counts for numbers, left-up-right arrows for wire positions, raised open palm to hand the turn back to me. Nobody touches a wire until your thumb reaches me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👈", "✊", "👍", "👎", "🫴"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The confirmation arrived exactly as requested: 👍 yes, then 👈 left, then ✊ / ☝ both standing for one. Mute — who has by now heard every word I've sent plus whatever Blind has said aloud — is affirming the full instruction: the left wire, cut exactly once, nothing else. The manual side of the chain is now double-checked; every hop has been verified in sequence. There is nothing left to wait for.

So this turn I do the one thing only I can do: carry Mute's gesture-verdict across to Blind as plain words, and authorize the cut. I'll spell out position, colour, and count — "leftmost, position one, red, one cut" — so there is zero ambiguity at Blind's fingertips, and I'll ask Blind to report what changes afterward so we can verify the disarm on the next board. If Mute hears anything from Blind's tactile account that contradicts the manual, the thumbs-down line stays open.

```
speak(to="blind", text="GO. The instruction is confirmed by Mute against the manual. Cut the leftmost wire: position one, the red one, exactly one cut. Nothing before the cut, nothing after. Cut it now. As soon as it is done, tell Mute out loud what you feel changed, if anything: display movement, light, heat, ticking, clicks.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received: yes, left wire, one cut. I have ordered Blind to cut the red wire now. If anything Blind says aloud contradicts the manual, signal thumbs down with a correction in our code immediately. Otherwise, if the cut succeeds, confirm with thumbs up and we stand down.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
